input.text: You're entering Jingshan Park — and it holds the single best view in Beijing. This hill right in front of you is man-made: five peaks of soil dug out to create the moats of the Forbidden City directly to the south. Climb to the pavilion on top, turn around, and you'll see it — the entire Forbidden City, its golden roofs stretching to the horizon, laid out like a stage set. It also holds a tragic story. In 1644, as rebels stormed the city, the last Ming emperor, Chongzhen, fled into this park and hanged himself from a tree — and with him, the Ming dynasty ended. The tree standing today is a descendant of the original, marked with a plaque. Come at sunset if you can: first the panorama, then the drums of the city at dusk. Jingshan is where Beijing reveals its perfect geometry.
